A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTERACT study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the reordered dataset and additional-results appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original student-teacher experiments across five domains, including quiz performance, teacher-quality comparisons, borrowed interactions, and learning-gain prediction.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain original experimental results and add an experiment comparing relevant transcripts with randomly selected unrelated transcripts.

M1.justification: The student-teacher interaction procedure, static-lesson variants, conversation-history accumulation, and prompt templates remain unchanged. Revisions concern experimental controls and post hoc feature analysis, not the INTERACT learning procedure.

E1.justification: The same 1,347 contexts and five domains are retained. Appendix B.1 adds an evaluation scenario in which students receive transcripts about unrelated concepts from the same domain, extending coverage to irrelevant conversational input.

E2.justification: V2 Table 8 adds a random-transcript comparator against original transcripts for gpt-4o-mini students with and without lessons. The existing LLM lineup and comparisons involving static lessons, teacher strength, and borrowed interactions remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new transcript-control experiment samples 100 concept interactions per domain and randomly substitutes unrelated interactions. Section 4.5 changes the reported predictor set from 45 to 53 features and specifies gpt-4o-mini student-teacher configurations where v1 described each domain and LM configuration. The main interaction settings and default hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a targeted ablation testing whether models use transcript content. The retained learning-gain analysis is expanded with features including context coverage, quiz coverage, semantic alignment, sentiment, and instruction following. Existing teacher-quality, borrowed-interaction, and extended-dialogue analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for plotted results, and Student's t-tests. The new random-transcript results are also averaged across three seeds; this extends the existing reporting practice without establishing an increased run count or a new uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports accuracy losses with unrelated transcripts; for example, Movie Plots accuracy with a lesson falls from 73.94 to 34.21. Section 4.5 replaces the reported maximum R-squared of 0.17 on Movie Plots with 0.14 on Song Lyrics and changes the leading predictors. These are findings under revised analysis settings, not a same-setting performance decline. Existing main performance tables and figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: The conceptual formulation is retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs. The expanded feature table supplies operational descriptions for empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims: the INTERACT framework, the five-domain benchmark, improved learning through interaction, matching static baselines in some five-turn settings, and reduced disadvantages from weaker teachers.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds the interpretation that students effectively use observed interactions, supported by deterioration when transcripts become irrelevant. The existing interpretations of teacher quality and borrowed interactions, and limitations concerning quiz-based evaluation, retention, and scalability, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code and data release; v2 announces availability and supplies a repository link in the first-page footnote. V2 Table 12 also identifies implementations for added analysis features and replaces the unanswered-query placeholder with GPT-4o-based assessment. Existing prompts and default hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds connections to document-grounded dialogue through doc2dial and MultiDoc2Dial, plus a human-tutoring discussion citing Bloom and VanLehn. The feature table additionally cites Bloom and Krathwohl's taxonomy. These five added references broaden context without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. V2 adds related-work passages and acknowledgements, revises the RQ5 account, swaps the dataset-creation and additional-results appendices, and makes small acronym and author-contact edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds the interaction-utilization table and expands the feature table, while relocating and renumbering several existing tables. Figure content remains unchanged, with page reflow and some relocation. The expanded feature table is crowded enough that its final rows share the footer area.

improvement.justification: The unrelated-transcript ablation supplies a useful missing control supporting actual use of conversational content. Expanded analysis details, additional research context, and reported code/data access improve documentation and reproducibility. These gains are limited: the central method and benchmark results remain unchanged, feature-based prediction remains weak, and the expanded feature table introduces minor layout crowding.
